title: Developer accepts AI-generated code fast, then spends longer proving the almost-right parts are safe
job: Use AI to increase throughput without shifting hidden verification and rework cost downstream.
trigger: AI generates a code change that looks plausible enough to merge or review.
surfaceComplaint: AI makes me faster until I have to debug the code it almost got right.
believedCause: The model just needs to get smarter.
mechanism: Generation speed has increased faster than verification capacity. Plausible output expands code volume while confidence remains weak, moving effort from typing to review, tests and debugging.

workflow.friction: verification can exceed saved generation time

economics.painCostNote: Stack Overflow reports 66% cite 'almost right' AI output as a major frustration and 45% say debugging AI-generated code takes more time.

buyer.roiLogic: One avoided debugging hour per developer per month can justify spend.

distribution.acquisition: The AI-authored diff is an explicit artifact and trigger.

competitors.gap: may miss spec mismatch / AI assumptions

intervention.notBuildYet: Do not generate another competing code diff.

experiment.artifactRequest: spec/prompt if available + diff + review + CI + bugs
experiment.outreach: teams with heavy AI coding use
experiment.success: ≥20% reduction in review/debug time or escaped AI defects without slower merges
experiment.kill: existing tests capture nearly all issues or AI authorship cannot be observed

claims.text: Stack Overflow reports 66% of developers are frustrated by AI solutions that are almost right.
More developers distrust AI accuracy than trust it in the 2025 survey.
Verification may become a larger opportunity as AI-generated code volume grows.
